issue_context.title: @parcel/transformer-svg-react "Namespace tags are not supported by default" error
issue_context.body:
While diagnosing #6362 (importing the `logo.svg` file attached to that issue), I ran into the "Namespace tags are not supported by default" error mentioned in gregberge/svgr#271.

If I run the svgr CLI and generate a React component manually, via `npx @svgr/cli logo.svg > Logo.jsx`, I'm able to use the resulting module without issue.  But if I do `import Logo from './logo.svg'`, I get the error in the title. 

What's the best way to resolve this?  The error message suggests setting `throwIfNamespace: false`.  But how/where do I do that?    (Is this a .babelrc thing?  If so, how do I set that up without being taken down the path of having to install a bunch of parcel and babel plugins and presets just to get back to the current baseline functionality Parcel provides?

[Edit to add...]

> If I run the svgr CLI and generate a React component manually, via npx @svgr/cli logo.svg > Logo.jsx, I'm able to use the resulting module without issue

That CLI runs svgo by default, which would explain the difference in behaviour if you just run the svg-react transformer.

review_comments:
What happens when `if (configFile)` evaluates to `false`? The function does not handle this case and it triggered this line: https://github.com/svg/svgo/blob/77102ed0963a5f1597e8072536311b55465e1874/lib/svgo.js#L21

I encountered this issue on parcel 2.0.0-rc.0. I have SVG, but I don't have a corresponding SVG Optimizer config. I do not have .parcelrc overrides.

I've opened https://github.com/svg/svgo/pull/1573. Sounds like you could be seeing what I've just found, which is actually https://github.com/svg/svgo/blob/721a1e591da131affece29362cf7e7089b474904/lib/svgo-node.js#L57-L59 (which doesn't have the null-ish check).
